title: Lesson Plan — Arithmetic Progressions (Class 10 NIOS Mathematics)
subject: Mathematics
objectives: Recognise an arithmetic progression and identify its first term a and common difference d.
Apply the n-th-term formula a_n = a + (n − 1) d to find a specific term, the position of a known term, or d.
Apply S_n = (n/2)(2 a + (n − 1) d) and S_n = (n/2)(a + l) to compute the sum of the first n terms of an AP.
Compute the arithmetic mean of two numbers and insert n arithmetic means between two given numbers.
Translate short word problems (savings, ladder rungs, theatre seating) into AP set-ups and solve them.
prerequisites: Class 9 manipulation of linear equations and substitution into formulas.
Comfort with positive and negative integers and basic arithmetic of fractions.
Solving simple simultaneous linear equations (needed for the 'two-given-terms' problem).
Quadratic equations from Chapter 6 (needed for the loan-instalment word problem).
materials: Whiteboard and markers (one colour reserved for d and S_n)
Reference card listing a_n and the two S_n forms, one per pair
Set of 'spot-the-AP' cards (mix of APs, GPs and quadratic sequences) for the Engage phase
Calculator (one per pair) for the larger sums

activities.description: Spot-the-AP card warm-up: students receive 6 short sequences (e.g. 5, 8, 11, 14; 2, 4, 8, 16; 1, 4, 9, 16; 25, 22, 19, 16; 1, 1, 2, 3, 5; 100, 110, 120, 130) and decide which are APs and which are not. Disagreements surface the precise definition: 'successive differences must all be equal'.
teacher_actions: Distribute cards; give 3 minutes for sorting.
Pick two pairs to share their tricky cards (especially 1, 4, 9, 16 — squares).
Tease: 'Today we'll learn how to leap to the 100th term of any AP without writing the rest.'
student_actions: Sort cards with bench partner; flag any they disagree on.
Be ready to defend their classification in 1 sentence.

activities.description: Pair task: each pair gets the AP 5, 8, 11, 14, … and is asked to find the 50th term WITHOUT writing all 50 terms. Most groups will spot the pattern '50th term = first term + 49 × common difference'. The teacher uses this discovery to motivate the formula a_n = a + (n − 1) d.
teacher_actions: Write the AP on the board.
Listen for 'add 3 forty-nine times' formulations and bring them up in the Explain phase.
Note who tries induction and who tries pattern-spotting.
student_actions: Try at least two strategies to find a_50.
Be ready to share your reasoning, not just the answer.

activities.description: Direct instruction in three short blocks: (i) state the AP definition, derive a_n = a + (n − 1) d by inspection, work three examples (find a_12; find AP given two terms; find which term equals 205); (ii) Gauss's pairing trick to derive S_n = (n/2)(2 a + (n − 1) d) and the equivalent S_n = (n/2)(a + l), work two examples (sum of first 30 terms of 2, 5, 8, …; sum 1 + 2 + … + 100); (iii) define arithmetic mean, derive the 'insert n means' formula d = (b − a)/(n + 1), and work one example (insert 3 means between 4 and 24).
teacher_actions: Build a 'two-formulae card' on the board side-by-side: a_n on the left, S_n on the right.
Live-derive S_n using Gauss's forward + backward addition trick.
After each example, ask which formula was the right one to pick and why.
student_actions: Take notes; replicate each worked example in their notebook.
Add a_n and the two S_n forms to a 'rules box' for quick reference.
Flag any step in the Gauss derivation they want re-explained.

activities.description: Application station: students work through six problems from the worksheet — two n-th-term problems, one 'how many three-digit multiples of 7' problem, two sum problems (one with l given, one without), and one short word problem (theatre seating). The teacher circulates and prompts students who get stuck to verbalise their first step.
teacher_actions: Circulate; offer the smallest hint that unblocks a student.
Watch for the common slip 'a + n d' instead of 'a + (n − 1) d'.
Pair fast finishers with peers who need support.
student_actions: Solve the six problems individually, showing all steps.
Self-check the first three against the posted answer key.
Ask a peer before asking the teacher.

activities.description: Exit-ticket quiz: an 8-question MCQ + short-answer slip with at least one item per content area, drawn from the chapter's question bank. Students complete it silently in 9 minutes; the teacher then projects the answers and runs a 4-minute discussion focused on the two items most students missed.
teacher_actions: Distribute the exit-ticket; remind students it is individual work.
Time the quiz to 9 minutes strictly.
Quickly tally results and address the top two miss items.
student_actions: Self-mark and write a one-line reflection on any item they got wrong.

activities.description: Set homework: complete the rest of the worksheet, plus one CREATE-level prompt from the bank ('Construct an AP whose 7th term is 23 and 11th term is 39, and write its first six terms and S_6'). Preview the next chapter (Percentage and its Applications) by writing 12.5% = 1/8 on the board and noting the link to ratios and proportions.
teacher_actions: Announce homework due date and the CREATE prompt.
Bridge to the next chapter with the 12.5% = 1/8 example.
student_actions: Pack the worksheet for home study.

homework: Complete the remaining problems on the Worksheet — Arithmetic Progressions handout.
Complete one CREATE-level prompt: construct an AP whose 7th term is 23 and 11th term is 39; write the first six terms and compute S_6 using both formulas as a check.
Find a real-world AP (savings plan, instalment-buying ad, ladder, seating chart) and write it as an AP with explicit a and d in your notebook.
assessment_ideas: Use the 8-item exit ticket described in the Evaluate phase as a quick formative check.
Set a 12-question MCQ quiz drawn from the chapter's question bank for the next class as a summative assessment.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER 'theatre seating with 30 rows' problem using the auto-grade rubric.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading round on the CREATE homework using a two-criterion rubric (a, d correct? S_6 matches both formulas?).
references: NIOS Secondary Mathematics, Module 1, Lesson 7: Arithmetic Progressions.
NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 5: Arithmetic Progressions (for additional worked examples).
